chunk_map.heading: The designer's piece: a prototype that answers one question

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1-7: "believe one works more than it does" — "one" and "it" resolve to "a prototype" in the same sentence chain (L3); "the finished look" (L7) is named by "How finished it looks" (L5). Closest: "which question it explores, and which it does not" (L5), antecedent "a prototype" L3.
L1-7: no pointer to another file by position; Houde and Hill named by name and year (L3).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1-7: no "the X you did/saw" backward reference to a beat; only the cited paper and "With agents" (L7).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no live-demo beat, guess cue or reveal on the slide

rules_evaluated.evidence: L1-7: single chunk carrying a self-contained claim (what a prototype is, the three questions, the over-belief warning, the agents closer); closest to thin is the 1-sentence closer L7, which is a paragraph of the same slide, not its own chunk.

L1 header "a prototype that answers one question" vs L3 "integration prototype brings all three together": closest to contradicting; the maintainer block (L14) attests "One question" is the designer's move on the day, not Houde and Hill's rule, and L7 says "the one question a prototype should answer" in the same register.

L3-7: no "Not X. Not Y. Z."; no anaphora triple; no self-grading superlative ("the hardest to build" L3 is the cited authors' claim, backing claim integration-prototype, not the deck grading itself); no number+retraction; no abstraction-noun stack ("the finished look" L7 is concrete); no verb triplet. Closest: L7 "got cheap ... did not" is a two-leg contrast, not a tic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1-7: no repo/authorial vocabulary in body; closest "The designer's piece" (L1) uses piece as an ordinary noun for a part of the day, not maintainer dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c "\*\*" over body L1-7 → 0 bold; budget of ≤1 met.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: curriculum/lectures/apt101-each-of-you-makes-something.md:5 carries the standalone include line [..](slides/prototype-to-learn.md); a slide file is inlined before any reader, so the ## reaches the composed deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/slides/prototype-to-learn.md → "OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent", exit 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/slides/prototype-to-learn.md → "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers", exit 0; grep -Ei "above|below|earlier|following" over body → 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links on the slide

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/slides/prototype-to-learn.md → slides: 1, oversized: 0, exit 0 (limits 210 words / 6 bullets).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1 "The designer's piece: a prototype that answers one question" is a claim heading on a lecture slide; the claim requirement binds law slides and this one states it. Closest: "The designer's piece:" prefix reads as an orientation label, which the rule exempts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L7 "With agents, the finished look got cheap. Picking the one question a prototype should answer did not." — closest to class (c) kicker echoing the header, but it adds the training's frame (agents made finish cheap, choosing the question did not), which no earlier sentence holds (backing claim agents-make-polish-cheap). No bullets; each paragraph adds a move.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1 header vs body: git log shows no header-only change; body answers the header (a prototype answers a question; which question; tell the audience). No inherited bullets answering an older header.
